sentences.text: Texasetes was a small, compact herbivore belonging to the ankylosaurian dinosaurs that lived in North America.
This armored quadruped grew to about 3 meters long and 1.2 meters tall, weighing roughly 550 kilograms.
Its body was protected by osteoderms on the back and limbs, supported by a horizontally oriented ilium and ankylosaurian shoulder features.
Named by Coombs in 1995, the genus was recovered from the Paw Paw Formation near Haslet in Tarrant County, Texas.
The holotype specimen USNM 337987 includes a skull fragment, teeth, vertebrae, partial limbs, and osteoderms, suggesting the animal died near a river or shore.
The animal belongs to the dinosaur class Ornithischia and is classified within the family Nodosauridae, with the type species Texasetes pleurohalio.
Its cervical vertebrae are concave, a trait shared with Animantarx that might be a unique feature for both.
Texasetes lived approximately 100 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Middle Cretaceous.
It is debated whether Pawpawsaurus is a synonym of Texasetes, though a 2016 analysis found them closer to different relatives.
While Coombs assigned the specimen to Nodosauridae, Vickaryous et al. consider the phylogenetic position of Texasetes to be uncertain within Ankylosauria.
A 2016 analysis also determined that a juvenile ankylosaurian skeleton from the same formation was more closely related to Niobrarasaurus than to either Pawpawsaurus or Texasetes.
